263.name: TypeScript compiler
263.notes: INSTALLED AND MEASURED in technology-universe/runtimes/javascript-text (npm, --save-exact) at 7.0.2. Smoke test passed via the CLI, and it surfaced a breaking change that belongs in every dependent's notes. ./node_modules/.bin/tsc reports 'Version 7.0.2' and compiled 'export const f=(x:number):string=>`${x}`' to 'export const f = (x) => `${x}`;' correctly. BUT TypeScript 7 is the Go-based native port, and the npm package's default export is now only ./lib/version.cjs exposing {version, versionMajorMinor} — ts.transpileModule, ts.ScriptTarget and ts.createProgram are GONE from the default import (measured: typeof ts.transpileModule === 'undefined'). The programmatic API moved to subpath exports under typescript/unstable/* (typescript/unstable/sync exposes 32 functions). Any tool doing `import ts from 'typescript'; ts.transpileModule(...)` breaks on 7.x. This is the single highest-impact upgrade hazard measured in this range.  ||  PRE-INSTALL RESEARCH: Upstream latest at probe time: 7.0.2, licence Apache-2.0. 268.name: PDFKit
268.notes: INSTALLED AND MEASURED in technology-universe/runtimes/javascript-text (npm, --save-exact) at 0.19.1. 269.name: MuPDF
269.notes: INSTALLED AND MEASURED via Homebrew at 1.28.2. `mutool -v` reports 1.28.2 (brew formula mupdf-tools, 102 MB in Cellar). Smoke test passed: `mutool draw -F txt` extracted 'REGISTRY SMOKE' from the fixture PDF and `mutool draw -o mu-out.png -r 100` rasterised it to a 7.4K PNG. Installing it locally for measurement creates no distribution obligation — the AGPL analysis below applies the moment you ship or expose it.  ||  PRE-INSTALL RESEARCH: Homebrew formula available: `mupdf-tools` (and `mupdf`), stable 1.28.2 per `brew info` — that is the formula's advertised version, not a measurement of an install here. Licensing is the headline and it is not benign: MuPDF is dual-licensed by Artifex under AGPL-3.0-or-later OR a paid commercial licence. AGPL obligations attach and they are stronger than GPL — if MuPDF is reachable over a network by users, the AGPL section 13 network clause requires you to offer those users the complete corresponding source of your application, not just of MuPDF. This is emphatically not an unrestricted permissive dependency. If you cannot meet that, you must buy the Artifex commercial licence. Same Artifex dual-licence structure applies to PyMuPDF (id 271). Review with counsel before shipping.

270.name: Poppler
270.notes: INSTALLED AND MEASURED via Homebrew at 26.08.0. CORRECTED MEASUREMENT — read this before trusting an earlier value. Poppler was 26.06.0 at the start of this session and was silently upgraded to 26.08.0 as a transitive dependency of another brew install partway through. Re-measured after the fact: `pdftotext -v` and `pdftoppm -v` both report 26.08.0, /opt/homebrew/opt/poppler symlinks to Cellar/poppler/26.08.0, and both kegs are still on disk. Smoke test re-run against the NEW binary and passed: pdftotext extracted 'REGISTRY SMOKE' and pdftoppm -png -r 100 produced a valid 7.7K PNG. The lesson generalises — a measured version is only true as of its measurement, and shared package managers move underneath you.  ||  PRE-INSTALL RESEARCH: INSTALLED AND VERIFIED ON THIS MACHINE. Version 26.06.0 measured two independent ways: `pdftotext -v` and `pdftoppm -v` both report 26.06.0, and `brew list --versions` reports poppler 26.06.0. Smoke test ran and passed: a PDF was generated with pycairo, `pdftotext` extracted the exact expected string 'REGISTRY SMOKE' from it, and `pdftoppm -png -r 150` rasterised the same PDF to a valid 834x417 PNG. Both read and render paths work. Hence P3, not P2. Licence: GPL-2.0-or-later. This is copyleft and it has teeth for redistribution — parts of poppler descend from Xpdf and are GPL-2.0, so linking it into a distributed closed-source product requires legal review. Using the CLI tools as separate subprocesses is a materially different position from linking libpoppler; know which one you are doing.

271.name: PyMuPDF

Both text and render paths confirmed. This does not soften the AGPL position below — it works, and that is precisely why the licence needs reading.  ||  PRE-INSTALL RESEARCH: Upstream latest on PyPI at probe time: 1.28.2. PyPI declares the licence as 'Dual Licensed - GNU AFFERO GPL 3.0 or Artifex Commercial Licence' — read verbatim from the package metadata, not inferred. AGPL obligations attach, including the section 13 network clause: a web service that uses PyMuPDF must offer its users the complete corresponding source. Not an unrestricted dependency. This is the Python binding over MuPDF (id 269) and inherits its terms. It is fast and capable, which is exactly why teams adopt it without reading the licence — do not repeat that. If AGPL is unacceptable, pypdf (id 272, BSD-3-Clause) and Poppler's CLI (id 270) are the usual permissive fallbacks.

272.name: pypdf
272.notes: INSTALLED AND MEASURED in technology-universe/runtimes/python-doc (isolated venv, Python 3.14.7) at 6.16.1. Pure Python: it reads, splits, merges and writes PDFs but does not rasterise or render, and it is slower than PyMuPDF (id 271). The trade is speed for a permissive licence, which is usually the right trade.

273.name: Apache Tika
273.notes: INSTALLED AND MEASURED via Homebrew at 3.3.2. Smoke test passed, using a JDK that was already on this machine but invisible: `java -version` on PATH hits the macOS stub and fails, but Homebrew's keg-only openjdk at /opt/homebrew/opt/openjdk/bin/java is OpenJDK 26.0.2. Homebrew also carries a `tika` formula, stable 3.3.2 per `brew info` (not installed), and `apache/tika` is an official Docker image — that image is usually the least painful route. Licence caveat worth reading before redistribution: Tika itself is Apache-2.0, but `tika-parsers` pulls in a large set of third-party format parsers whose licences vary and are not all Apache-2.0. Audit the actual dependency tree you ship. A PyPI package named `tika` (latest 3.3.2) also exists but it is only a thin REST client for a running Tika server, not the engine.

274.name: OpenCV
274.notes: INSTALLED AND MEASURED in technology-universe/runtimes/python-doc (isolated venv, Python 3.14.7) at 5.0.0.93. Smoke test passed on arm64 — the install the coordinator flagged as at-risk did NOT fail. cv2.__version__ reports build 5.0.0; imread returned a (40,90,3) array, resize produced (20,45,3), and cvtColor produced a (20,45) grayscale. Installed from the prebuilt cp37-abi3-macosx_13_0_arm64 wheel (48.3 MB), no compilation needed. IMPORTANT: the installed major version is 5.x, comfortably inside the Apache-2.0 era, so the licence field is correct for this pin.  ||  PRE-INSTALL RESEARCH: Upstream latest on PyPI at probe time: 5.0.0.93 for `opencv-python`, PyPI licence field 'Apache 2.0'. Pin carefully, because the licence changed with the version: OpenCV is Apache-2.0 from 4.5.0 onward, but releases before that are BSD-3-Clause. Recording a bare 'OpenCV is Apache-2.0' would be wrong for any 4.4-or-earlier pin, so the licence here is only valid for 4.5+ — if you pin an older release, re-record it as BSD-3-Clause. Second trap in the same family: `opencv-python` wheels bundle third-party codecs (FFmpeg among them) with their own terms, and the `opencv-contrib-*` packages add modules that include patent-encumbered algorithms (SIFT/SURF lineage) — choose between `opencv-python`, `opencv-python-headless`, `opencv-contrib-python` deliberately. Headless is the right default for servers and containers. This record is the canonical one; id 288 repeats OpenCV in category 22 and points here.

275.name: Pillow
275.notes: INSTALLED AND MEASURED in technology-universe/runtimes/python-doc (isolated venv, Python 3.14.7) at 12.3.0. Smoke test passed: created a 90x40 RGB image, wrote and reopened it as PNG with size/mode intact, and resized to 30x13. Import name is `PIL`.  ||  PRE-INSTALL RESEARCH: Upstream latest on PyPI at probe time: 12.3.0, licence expression MIT-CMU. MIT-CMU (the HPND-style licence Pillow inherited from PIL) is permissive — noted precisely rather than rounded to 'MIT' because the SPDX identifier differs. Friendly fork of the dead PIL; import name is `PIL`, package name is `Pillow`. Pillow has a steady stream of CVEs in its image decoders, so keep it current wherever it touches untrusted uploads.

276.name: ImageMagick
276.notes: INSTALLED AND MEASURED via Homebrew at 7.1.2-29. `magick --version` reports ImageMagick 7.1.2-29 Q16-HDRI aarch64 (28 MB in Cellar). Smoke test passed: resized the fixture PNG to 40px wide and converted to grayscale, with `magick identify` confirming '40x12 Gray'. Note ImageMagick 7 uses the single `magick` binary — the old `convert` and `identify` commands are not installed as separate executables here.  ||  PRE-INSTALL RESEARCH: `version` is therefore null. Homebrew formula `imagemagick` is available, stable 7.1.2-29 per `brew info` (formula metadata, not a measurement of an install here). On Debian/Ubuntu the apt package is `imagemagick`. Licence is the ImageMagick Licence (SPDX id `ImageMagick`), a permissive Apache-2.0-derived text — permissive, but not literally Apache-2.0, so record it by its own name. Security note that matters operationally: ImageMagick has a long history of delegate-based RCE (the ImageTragick class of bugs). If it ever touches user-uploaded files, harden `policy.xml` and disable the delegates you do not need. libvips (id 278) is generally faster and lower-memory for pure resize/convert pipelines.

277.name: Sharp
277.notes: INSTALLED AND MEASURED in technology-universe/runtimes/javascript-text (npm, --save-exact) at 0.35.3. Smoke test passed end to end: created a 120x80 RGB surface, encoded PNG, resized to 30x20, re-encoded JPEG, and metadata confirmed 30x20 jpeg. The prebuilt darwin-arm64 binary and its bundled libvips resolved correctly. npm audit clean. Reminder from the licence note below: the bundled libvips is LGPL-2.1-or-later even though sharp itself is Apache-2.0.  ||  PRE-INSTALL RESEARCH: Upstream latest at probe time: 0.35.3, licence Apache-2.0. Node binding over libvips (id 278). Two consequences worth recording: sharp's own code is Apache-2.0 but the bundled libvips is LGPL-2.1-or-later, so the dependency you actually ship carries LGPL terms — dynamic linking keeps that manageable, static linking does not, and a redistribution review should look at the whole artifact, not just sharp's LICENSE file. Second: it installs prebuilt platform-specific binaries, so lockfiles built on macOS can fail on Linux CI and on serverless targets with a different libc — build the deployment artifact on the target platform.

278.name: libvips
278.notes: INSTALLED AND MEASURED via Homebrew at 8.18.5. `vips --version` reports vips-8.18.5 (brew keg 8.18.5_1, 6.2 MB — by far the smallest of the image stacks measured here). Smoke test passed: `vips resize` scaled the 900x260 fixture by 0.25 and vipsheader confirmed the output as '225x65 uchar, 3 bands, srgb'.  ||  PRE-INSTALL RESEARCH: Homebrew formula `vips` is available, stable 8.18.5 per `brew info` (formula metadata, not a local measurement). Licence is LGPL-2.1-or-later — weaker copyleft than GPL, but not permissive: dynamic linking is fine for closed-source use, static linking triggers relinking obligations. This is the licence that reaches through sharp (id 277) into Node projects. Demand-driven, streaming architecture keeps memory flat on very large images, which is why it beats ImageMagick (id 276) on throughput. Also the usual tiler for OpenSeadragon (id 266).

279.name: scikit-image

Complements rather than replaces OpenCV (id 274): scikit-image is more readable and NumPy-native, OpenCV is faster for real-time work. Pulls in NumPy and SciPy, so the install is not small.

280.name: imageio

281.name: Wand
281.notes: INSTALLED AND MEASURED in technology-universe/runtimes/python-doc (isolated venv, Python 3.14.7) at 0.7.2. 282.name: torchvision
